part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Opening Ranges: Time, Boundaries and Context
quote: Build a time-and-price reference before choosing a pattern. A scheduled open is certain; its direction is not.

sections.title: What is an ICT opening range?
sections.content: An opening range is the highest and lowest traded price within a stated time window. It is not the first candle, the opening price alone, or a gap across a market closure. In this study, the New York morning window is 09:30–10:00. Mark its opening price immediately, but treat its high and low as developing until the window ends. A level drawn at 09:35 must not use a high first printed at 09:52.

sections.title: Which session windows should you study?
sections.content: Keep five references distinct: midnight 00:00–00:30, the Venom reference 08:00–09:30, the cash-opening study 09:30–10:00, the afternoon opening study 13:30–14:00, and the final cash-session context approaching 16:00. These are New York local times. The 08:00 range is a pre-open reference, not another stock-exchange opening. The final hour and market-on-close discussion are context, not interchangeable thirty-minute opening ranges. Different models use different parts of this clock.

sections.title: Worked example: freeze the range before judging the break
sections.content: Suppose the 09:30 opening price is 100. By 09:40, observed prices span 98–103. At 09:52 a new high reaches 106. The completed range at 10:00 is therefore 98–106, with midpoint 102. An excursion to 107 is above that completed range. A return below 106 is a different observation from sustained trading above it. Neither outcome, by itself, identifies a profitable entry. The first presented FVG adds a selection question; liquidity context adds a possible objective.

sections.title: How do daylight saving, holidays and feeds change the study?
sections.content: Use the America/New_York timezone and the actual exchange calendar, rather than a fixed EST offset. The normal NYSE core session is 09:30–16:00 Eastern, with calendar exceptions. Futures can trade outside that cash session. Record contract month, chart session, aggregation and data provider. Do not combine an ETH premarket high from one feed with an RTH low from another without labelling the difference. If a holiday changes the session, adapt the observation plan before the day, not after seeing its outcome.

sections.title: How to build a morning observation sheet
sections.content: Before 09:30, record the overnight and premarket extremes, the prior regular-session references and any scheduled release. At the open, note where price begins relative to those levels. During the window, update only the prices already observed. After 10:00, freeze the range and classify the subsequent response as acceptance, rejection or unresolved. Finally, ask whether a separate model offered a recognised entry before the selected objective was reached. This sequence prevents a common mistake: seeing the completed day, drawing an opening box, and assuming every later reaction to it was tradable.

sections.title: Compare the morning with the afternoon fairly
sections.content:
Use the same measurement method when comparing 09:30–10:00 with 13:30–14:00, but keep their samples separate. A wide morning range and a narrow afternoon range create different distances to a midpoint or boundary. Report distances in the instrument’s points and ticks before translating them into monetary risk. The two windows also begin with different available information: the afternoon already has the morning’s path. Copying a morning interpretation into the afternoon without checking the current objective ignores that difference.

Before adding entry rules, compare the first presented FVG lesson and the Venom model. Use Chart Laboratory to practise identifying what is visible before the range completes.

keyTerms.definition: The high–low interval observed within declared start and end times.
A window whose final high and low are not known yet.
The first observed price at the declared session boundary, distinct from a timed high–low range.
Sustained trading beyond a reference under a declared observation rule, rather than a momentary excursion.

summary: Declare the session and timezone before measuring.
Freeze the range only after its final candle completes.
Compare continuation, rejection and unresolved outcomes.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Midnight Range, RTH Gaps and NWOG
quote: Three references, three measurements: a timed range, a daily reopening gap and a weekly reopening gap.

sections.title: Midnight opening range versus opening price
sections.content: The midnight opening price is the first price of the selected New York date. The midnight opening range in this study spans 00:00–00:30. Its high, low and opening price are separate references. If prices during that window range from 200 to 208, the midpoint is 204 and quarter levels are 202 and 206. A later revisit to 204 is a midpoint test, not proof that midnight created a permanent support or resistance level.

sections.title: How do you measure an RTH opening gap?
sections.content: An RTH opening gap compares the selected previous regular-session closing reference with the next regular-session opening price. For a close of 100 and next open of 108, the interval is 100–108; its midpoint is 104. The gap size is eight points, even if the first half-hour range is 106–112. A futures chart’s last RTH bar is not automatically the exchange settlement price. State the exact session template and closing convention. Do not substitute a stock-market close for a futures reference without explanation.

sections.title: What is a new week opening gap?
sections.content: NWOG compares the last quoted price before the weekend closure with the first quoted price after reopening, using one instrument and feed. FX broker quotes and futures exchange sessions differ; do not apply one Sunday opening time to every product. A Friday close of 108 and Sunday open of 104 create a 104–108 reference with midpoint 106. Weekday overnight gaps, an RTH gap and a three-candle fair value gap answer different questions. Keep their names and anchors visible on your chart.

sections.title: Gap tests: partial return, full traversal and no return
sections.content: With an upward 100–108 gap, a decline to 106 tests the upper quarter; 104 reaches the midpoint; 100 traverses the full reference. Price can stop at any of these points, cross the interval, or never return. An unvisited older gap remains historical context, not a debt the market must repay. Before replay, choose which gaps remain displayed, when they expire and whether a wick or a close counts as crossing a boundary. Otherwise an increasingly crowded chart makes almost any outcome look predicted.

sections.title: A downward gap uses the same arithmetic
sections.content: For a previous closing reference of 212 and a new opening price of 204, the interval is 204–212. The midpoint is 208; quarters are 206 and 210. On a rise from the new opening side, 206 is the first quarter reached, 208 the middle and 212 the far boundary. The quarter labels describe location, not an instruction to buy or sell. When several daily and weekly gaps overlap, label each by its formation date and keep its own anchors; combining them into one unexplained rectangle loses the original measurements.

sections.title: Choose which historical gaps remain relevant
sections.content:
Write a retention rule before study: for example, display the current NWOG and a specified number of earlier weekly gaps, with daily gaps tracked separately. That is an organisational choice, not an authenticated universal ICT expiry rule. If you change the rule later, preserve the original test and label the new version. Add the actual amount of traversal and the time it occurred to the journal. A market that crosses a midpoint five times differs from a clean first revisit even when the same horizontal level appears on both charts.

Compare this measurement with the first presented FVG lesson: a reopening gap and a three-candle imbalance are different references. Chart Laboratory helps practise the candle geometry separately.

keyTerms.definition: The interval between the selected weekly closing and reopening quotes.
Levels at 25%, 50% and 75% of a declared price interval.
The selected prior regular-session closing price compared with the next regular-session opening price.
The high and low of the chosen 00:00–00:30 New York observation window.

summary: Do not confuse a timed range with a reopening gap.
Record the feed and closing-price convention.
Count partial, complete and absent returns separately.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: First Presented FVG: Timing and Qualification
quote: Find the first qualifying imbalance, not simply the first attractive three-candle shape.

sections.title: What makes the first presented FVG qualify?
sections.content: A bullish fair value gap exists when candle 1 high is below candle 3 low after candle 3 completes; reverse the inequality for a bearish gap. That geometry is only the first check. First-presented selection also asks whether the candidate departs from the preceding balanced area in the chosen session and direction. A geometrically valid gap can therefore be rejected for this particular model without ceasing to be an FVG. Mark the preceding range before choosing the candidate, rather than redrawing it around the winner.

sections.title: Does the rule always start at 09:31?
sections.content: The basic one-minute morning study selects a qualifying FVG in the 09:31–10:00 New York window. The advanced 09:30 treatment uses additional opening-gap and preceding-liquidity context; it is not permission to relabel every opening imbalance. A candle stamped 09:30 is still forming until 09:31. A three-candle pattern is only confirmed when its third candle closes. Write both the bar timestamp and the recognition time so the exercise cannot use information from an unfinished candle.

sections.title: Worked selection: reject A, then evaluate B
sections.content: Assume the preceding balanced area is 99–104. Candidate A has outer-candle boundaries 101–102: a genuine bullish FVG, but entirely inside that area. Candidate B later has boundaries 104–106 following an upward departure; it is a different contextual candidate. Its consequent encroachment is 105. A subsequent low of 105.5 enters B without reaching a 105 midpoint order. A low of 104.5 passes the midpoint, but actual execution still depends on order type and available liquidity. Neither case earns a fictional fill.

sections.title: What ends the idea, and what if there is no retracement?
sections.content: Choose a reference, entry convention, failure condition, observation deadline and cost assumption before replay. A completed close below 104 could end a bullish 104–106 study under one stated rule; it is not a universal rule for all ICT models. If price leaves without returning to 105, record an unfilled idea rather than chasing it or awarding a win. Compare qualified failures, rejected gaps that later worked, and no-return moves. That comparison tests selection honestly and prevents first from becoming a synonym for best.

sections.title: Separate selection, entry and invalidation prices
sections.content: Selection identifies the interval. Entry chooses where, if anywhere, participation would be considered. Invalidation defines the event that ends the particular idea. These are three different decisions. For the invented 104–106 bullish interval, an edge study uses 106, a midpoint study 105, and a deeper study another predeclared price. They cannot share the same fill statistics. A stop chosen below the associated swing also differs from a rule ending the zone’s directional use after a close. State both rather than assuming a chart label supplies them automatically.

sections.title: Study the bearish mirror and rejected winners
sections.content:
A bearish example with candle 1 low 108 and candle 3 high 106 has boundaries 106–108 and midpoint 107. Check the preceding balance and bearish departure before accepting it in the chosen model. If a rejected inside-balance gap later reacts beautifully, keep that example: it tests the cost of the filter rather than invalidating the historical rejection. Compare it with accepted candidates that fail. A selection rule is evaluated across all its decisions, not defended by showing only the later move that agrees with it.

Combine the measurement with SMT and a declared PD array rather than treating a first gap as a complete trade. Use Trade Simulator to examine the difference between an observed setup and an actual entry condition.

keyTerms.definition: A geometrical gap that also meets the declared model context.
The earliest moment all information needed for a label is complete.
The midpoint of a declared FVG interval; reaching an edge is not reaching this midpoint.
A premarked area of overlapping two-way price delivery used as a contextual selection reference.

summary: Separate geometric validity from model qualification.
Use completed candles and record recognition time.
An unfilled midpoint is not a winning trade.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT PD Arrays: Range Selection and Price Delivery
quote: A chart full of rectangles is not a framework. Choose the range, then explain why a particular reference matters.

sections.title: Build the twenty-day dealing-range matrix
sections.content: Start with the most recent twenty completed trading days, not twenty calendar days. Mark the highest high and lowest low, then divide their interval into quarters. For a 100–140 range, equilibrium is 120 and quarter levels are 110 and 130. Price at 132 lies in the upper quarter of this selected range. Premium means above its midpoint; discount means below. Neither word means an asset is fundamentally expensive or cheap. The range anchors must remain visible because another valid range can change the classification.

sections.title: How do higher and lower timeframes connect?
sections.content: Locate a higher-timeframe objective and the relevant quadrant before refining a PD array on a lower timeframe. If a fifteen-minute FVG spans 120–126 but its upper half has already been traversed, do not call the entire interval untouched. Examine completed five-minute and one-minute candles to see which sub-interval remains a candidate. Return to the higher timeframe when new candles complete. A forty- or sixty-day lookback can be a separately labelled extension in a running market; switching anchors solely to fit an entry is hindsight.

sections.title: Classic FVG, suspension, inversion and reclaimed references
sections.content: A classic FVG compares outer wicks. A suspension reference instead examines body-price imbalances around a central candle; overlapping wicks do not automatically remove that body-based configuration. For example, a previous close of 100, central open/close of 102/106 and next open of 108 leave separate body gaps at 100–102 and 106–108. That is not proof of a classic 100–108 FVG. An inverse FVG changes directional use after a stated failure; a reclaimed reference returns to an earlier role after another change. These labels describe different histories.

sections.title: Worked contrast: relevant array versus attractive array
sections.content: Suppose your completed range is 100–140 and a bearish study begins near 134. A nearby premium reference at 132–134 fits that location; a bullish gap at 106–108 belongs to another part of the range. Neither wins merely by looking cleaner. Record which reference was known, how it had previously traded, and what would end its proposed role. A balanced price range is an overlap of specified opposing intervals, not a guarantee of support. A low-resistance move may leave your chosen array unvisited; a crowded high-resistance path may justify no study entry.

sections.title: Use an actual hierarchy of references
sections.content: Start with the range and objective, then identify the relevant PD array and its internal geometry. An order block selects a candle or consecutive run; its opening price, body midpoint and full wick are different boundaries. A breaker adds a prior swing sequence and changed role. A rejection block emphasises a body reference attached to a rejection wick. FVG, IFVG, BPR and suspension describe other configurations. The hierarchy organises questions rather than proving that one rectangle always outranks another. Use the linked foundational chapters to apply each exact definition before combining references.

sections.title: Why an intermediate-term high is not just a new high
sections.content:
Structural labels depend on relationships among confirmed swings. Under a common nested comparison, an intermediate-term high is a selected short-term high with lower short-term highs on either side; the exact convention must be stated. The right-side comparison arrives later, so the label cannot be known at the central high’s first print. A higher-timeframe PD array may give that swing context, but does not erase confirmation delay. Link the swing hierarchy to the range map without pretending a final structural label was available at the turning candle.

Keep the higher-timeframe map separate from lower-timeframe execution. Chart Laboratory is the place to practise recognising individual references before combining them into one model.

keyTerms.definition: A range-relative map of selected price references across completed lookback periods.
Connecting completed higher-timeframe context to finer price references without using future bars.
The midpoint of the selected high–low interval; changing the anchors changes the level.
Selected body-price discontinuities adjacent to a central candle; not automatically a classic wick-based FVG.
A price reference returning to a prior directional role after an intervening role change.

summary: Keep the selected range and lookback explicit.
Distinguish wick geometry from body-gap conventions.
A relevant reference may never offer an entry.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: SMT Divergence: Compare Markets Without Guesswork
quote: Compare corresponding extremes in related markets. A disagreement is evidence to investigate, not an entry button.

sections.title: What is SMT divergence?
sections.content: SMT is a non-confirmation between specified extremes in related markets over aligned intervals. In a bearish comparison, one instrument exceeds its earlier high while another fails to exceed its corresponding high. A bullish comparison uses lows. Compare highs with highs and lows with lows; closing prices answer another question. The observation says the series behaved differently. It does not reveal which trader placed an order, prove hidden accumulation, or guarantee the instrument that lagged will lead the next move.

sections.title: Align the instruments before comparing them
sections.content: NQ and ES can be studied as related equity-index futures, but their price levels and constituent weights differ. Use the same interval, trading session, contract treatment and reliable timestamps. A spot FX quote and a futures chart can have different session boundaries. DXY and a USD-quoted currency pair may often move inversely, but that relationship is conditional. For an inverse comparison, state the expected high-to-low relationship explicitly rather than applying the same-direction high-to-high test without adjustment.

sections.title: Worked example: a divergence can disappear
sections.content: At the first reference, NQ high is 100 and ES high is 200. At the next completed observation, NQ reaches 102 while ES reaches 199. There is a high-based non-confirmation relative to those anchors, despite the different price scales. If ES later trades 201 inside your still-open observation window, both earlier highs have now been exceeded. The earlier snapshot remains real, but the continuing divergence claim no longer holds. Save the time of recognition, the end of the comparison window and the later change.

sections.title: Where does SMT fit in a complete study?
sections.content: First choose a meaningful liquidity reference and a directional scenario. Then evaluate the intermarket observation alongside displacement, a selected PD array and a separately defined entry and failure rule. A divergence at an arbitrary micro-swing is not equivalent to one at a preselected session extreme. Compare the same base setup with and without the SMT filter, including rejected winners and accepted losers. Until a properly defined sample demonstrates an improvement after costs, treat the filter as a hypothesis rather than an established advantage.

sections.title: Compare lows without reversing the logic by accident
sections.content: For a bullish comparison, suppose NQ’s earlier low is 100 and ES’s is 200. NQ later trades 98 while ES holds 201. NQ has broken its low while ES has not: a low-based non-confirmation. It is not automatically bullish for both instruments, and it does not tell you which one to buy. Record the chosen directional interpretation and the separate response you would need in the instrument under study. Inverse-market comparisons require their own explicitly inverted anchor relationship.

sections.title: Avoid correlation and contract-roll traps
sections.content:
A related-market pair is a hypothesis about comparable behaviour, not a permanent mechanical link. Index composition, currency drivers and trading hours can produce legitimate disagreement. Continuous futures may splice or adjust historical contracts, while a front-month chart preserves a specific contract’s prices. Do not compare an adjusted high on one chart with an unadjusted high on another and label the difference institutional intent. Save the actual symbols, contract conventions, date and observation fields so another learner can reproduce the comparison.

Apply the comparison alongside a selected opening range or liquidity sweep. In Backtest Lab, keep the same entry model while comparing observations with and without the SMT filter.

keyTerms.definition: One series exceeds an anchor extreme while the aligned comparison series does not.
The declared interval within which corresponding extremes are evaluated.
The preselected high or low against which each market’s later corresponding extreme is compared.
A hypothesised opposite-direction relationship requiring a different high-to-low comparison convention.

summary: Compare corresponding price fields and times.
Allow a later observation to remove the divergence.
SMT is context, not an independent execution model.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Liquidity: Turtle Soup and Rejection Blocks
quote: Separate a visible price reference from the orders you infer around it. Then examine the response after the break.

sections.title: Map liquidity references before the excursion
sections.content: Old highs, old lows and similar-looking extremes are visible references. Stops near them are a plausible hypothesis, not an order-book fact supplied by a candle. Mark whether the reference comes from the overnight session, premarket, RTH or a higher timeframe. A new RTH high is not identical to the full ETH high. Rank a nearby objective separately from a distant weekly objective so a small sweep is not mistaken for completion of the whole daily narrative.

sections.title: Turtle Soup: break, response and possible return
sections.content: A Turtle Soup-style study examines an excursion beyond a chosen old extreme followed by rejection back toward the prior range. The excursion alone is not the setup. For an old high of 110, a trade to 112 and return below 110 differs from sustained acceptance above 110. Define how rejection is recognised and whether a wick or completed close is required in your variation. Do not call every high break manipulation or every return a reversal that must continue.

sections.title: Deferred rejection-block entry versus selling the high
sections.content: A rejection block studies the opening/closing body reference associated with a rejection wick. Its body boundary and the full wick are different measurements. In a bearish teaching example, the excursion prints a body at 110–111 with high 112, then price departs to 107 and leaves a selected imbalance. A later return to the declared body reference is a deferred candidate; selling blindly at 110 before the rejection exists is another strategy. Entry, protective stop and objective still need separate rules, including what happens if no return occurs.

sections.title: Resistance paths and the source-specific Gauntlet idea
sections.content: A low-resistance liquidity run describes a relatively clear path through selected references; high resistance describes more opposing price structure. The classification depends on the timeframe and mapped arrays. The Gauntlet example is more specific: within a bullish breaker sequence, inspect the down-leg into the lower low and identify the relevant nearby SIBI and body-gap boundary before studying its changed use. It is not a name for any FVG overlap. If the required leg or boundary is unclear, leave the case unclassified instead of forcing a label.

sections.title: Rejection-block arithmetic and a contrasting stop location
sections.content:
In the invented 110–111 body with a 112 wick high, the body midpoint is 110.5. The midpoint of the full 110–112 span is 111. Those are not interchangeable mean references. A proposed return to 110.5, a stop beyond 112 and an objective at 106 create their own distance and cost assumptions. If the return occurs before the required rejection and departure are complete, it is too early for that deferred sequence. If it occurs after the declared expiry, it belongs to another study.

Read the order blocks and breaker blocks lessons before combining rejection references. Trade Simulator is useful for checking why a response and a later executable entry are separate events.

keyTerms.definition: An entry considered only after the required response and a later return are observable.
A declared body-price reference associated with a rejection wick.
A declared old-extreme excursion followed by a separately recognised rejection response.
A proposed route with more opposing mapped structure; the classification depends on timeframe and references.

summary: Label session-specific highs and lows separately.
Compare rejection with acceptance beyond the reference.
Do not force a deferred entry when no return occurs.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Venom Model: Range, Sweep and Two Fangs
quote: Study the opening-session Venom variant as a sequence, including the versions that never provide a deferred entry.

sections.title: Which range defines this Venom example?
sections.content: This opening-session variant freezes the 08:00–09:30 New York high and low on an extended-hours chart. The window is a reference, not a claim that every ninety-minute interval is a Venom setup. At 09:30, label the completed boundaries and the location of broader liquidity. A range of 100–110 gives two references; it does not prescribe whether the next move must attack the high, low or both. Other session variants require their own source and timing definition.

sections.title: What do the two fangs describe?
sections.content: In the bearish example, price moves above the range high and a candle closes above that buy-side reference. An inefficient upward departure is followed by an opposing inefficient move down: the two fangs. The downward response changes the interpretation of the earlier break. A wick above the high without the specified close is not the same version. Nor is a completed close above the high sufficient if price keeps accepting higher prices without the opposing response. The bullish mirror should be labelled as a teaching contrast, not substituted for the reviewed bearish example.

sections.title: Worked sequence: aggressive versus deferred participation
sections.content: Use an invented 100–110 reference range. A candle reaches 113 and closes 112; a later opposing move trades back below 110 and leaves a declared reference. An aggressive response-based idea and a deferred return to a selected Venom candle opening price have different recognition times and risk distances. Do not award the deferred entry at 111 unless a later price actually returns there after the reference is known. A move straight to 104 can support the directional reading while leaving the deferred order unfilled.

sections.title: Failure, expiry and the limits of the model name
sections.content: Define the protected extreme, the chosen entry boundary and the time at which the idea expires. Acceptance back above a selected bearish failure level can end the thesis; no retracement can end the opportunity without a loss. SMT, a breaker or an FVG may add context, but do not invent a mandatory five-stage chain that every Venom instance must contain. The range, candle-close condition and opposing departure are observable. Claims about who engineered them, fixed success rates or guaranteed full-range targets are not established by their appearance.

sections.title: Measure the consequences of waiting for a return
sections.content:
Suppose a deferred bearish example considers 111, with a hypothetical protective level at 114 and objective 104. The planned distance is three points of risk and seven points of reward, before costs and any slippage. Moving the entry down to 108 after the decline would leave six points to the same protective level and only four to the objective. That is a different plan, not the same setup at a slightly worse price. The example illustrates why a missed return cannot be repaired by quietly moving the entry.

The first presented FVG and SMT lessons explain optional contextual observations; they are not compulsory additions to every Venom variant. Practise a separately defined entry sequence in Trade Simulator.

keyTerms.definition: The explicitly selected pre-open high–low interval for this opening-session variant.
Opposing inefficient departures evaluated within the stated Venom context.
A separately defined response-based entry considered earlier than a deferred return; it has different risk assumptions.
A proposed later return to a selected reference after the required sequence is recognised.

summary: Freeze 08:00–09:30 before interpreting the excursion.
Separate a wick sweep from the reviewed closing condition.
A correct direction can still leave the entry unfilled.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Lunch and Afternoon Session Models
quote: Read the morning first. Lunch and afternoon references make sense only in relation to what has already happened.

sections.title: Choose the first prominent swing after 10:00
sections.content: In the lunch-retracement study, the morning direction determines which post-10:00 reference is relevant. After a directional morning decline, study the first prominent swing high formed after 10:00 as a possible retracement objective. After a strong morning advance, the corresponding swing low can serve that role. The first swing after the time boundary is not the absolute highest or lowest point selected at lunchtime. Define prominence with a swing rule and wait for its confirmation; do not move the anchor because another swing later looks better.

sections.title: Worked contrast: a retracement thesis versus continued decline
sections.content: Suppose the market declines from 110 to 100, forms a confirmed post-10:00 swing high at 104, and later fails to make a new low. A developing recovery toward 104 can be studied after a separately defined response. If price instead breaks 100 and continues lower, the same lunch-retracement story has not developed. A market structure shift needs an explicit swing and breach convention; not every educator requires the identical closing test. The clock alone does not override a fresh low or create an entry.

sections.title: The 13:30–14:00 afternoon opening range
sections.content: Treat 13:30–14:00 as a new observation window in this framework. Carry forward the morning’s completed references, then assess the afternoon location and objective. A morning bearish array can be reconsidered in an opposing afternoon scenario only after the relevant change is observed. It does not automatically flip roles at 13:30. The first presented afternoon FVG is a selection study with its own window; it is not permission to trade every imbalance left anywhere during the morning.

sections.title: Final-hour and market-on-close context
sections.content: Keep a named macro window such as 14:50–15:10 separate from the final cash-session context. The reviewed market-on-close discussion includes 15:45–16:00; that is an ICT study window, not a universal exchange auction timetable. Check the actual product’s closing procedure, calendar and early-close schedule. A futures contract can continue trading after the stock-market close. Late-session volatility, thin execution or a nearly completed objective can make observation more useful than inventing a final trade to finish the day.

sections.title: Keep swing confirmation and target availability separate
sections.content:
A high printed at 10:12 becomes a confirmed swing only after the required right-side evidence arrives. If your rule needs a later lower high, the target is not available for a decision made at 10:12 itself. Then distinguish reaching the reference from executing a trade toward it. A market may revisit 104 before your selected entry pattern completes, or leave no affordable return at all. Journal both the moment the objective became usable and the moment the entry became usable; a completed screenshot can hide this important ordering.

Compare the opening range lesson with the weekly profiles lesson to separate clock references from broader directional context. Keep any attempted execution as a distinct exercise in Trade Simulator.

keyTerms.definition: The first confirmed prominent swing of the declared type after the time boundary.
Reconsidering an earlier reference only after the specified contextual change occurs.
The high–low study window from 13:30 to 14:00 New York local time in this framework.
A late-session observation framework distinct from an exchange’s actual auction and closing rules.

summary: Do not choose the lunchtime anchor with hindsight.
The afternoon does not automatically reverse the morning.
Use the product calendar for closing procedures.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT News Days: Volatility and No-Trade Decisions
quote: A release changes the conditions of execution. A neat candle pattern does not remove event risk.

sections.title: Start with the event calendar, not a prediction
sections.content: Record the scheduled release, its actual date and New York time before the session. CPI and the Employment Situation are distinct releases; holidays can change familiar dates. An FOMC statement and a subsequent press conference are separate information events. Unscheduled geopolitical news cannot be handled by a calendar alone. The purpose is to identify when spreads, speed and available depth may differ from your ordinary replay assumptions, not to forecast the number or promise the first move will reverse.

sections.title: A two-stage event can produce opposite moves
sections.content: An initial decision can produce displacement, followed by a second move when later remarks change expectations. The second move may reverse or extend the first. Freeze each stage’s available information and avoid explaining the entire afternoon as one obvious signal. A large FVG formed during the first burst can be too wide for the declared risk plan, never retrace, or be traversed during the next stage. The existence of the gap does not establish that a resting order was safely executable.

sections.title: Worked execution example: the chart cannot resolve every fill
sections.content: A hypothetical long entry is 100, stop 98 and target 104. One later candle has high 105 and low 97. Those four OHLC values do not establish whether the target or stop traded first after entry. Mark the case ambiguous unless finer data resolves the sequence. A stop-market order can fill below 98 during a fast move; a stop-limit can remain unfilled. A backtest that assumes the target first and the stop exactly at 98 has added favourable facts the candle did not provide.

sections.title: What does a useful no-trade plan contain?
sections.content: Specify whether you will observe only, wait for a defined post-release interval, or require normal execution conditions before a simulation. There is no universally safe number of minutes. Record why the case was excluded and keep its later result, including the excluded move that would have looked profitable. A news filter can reduce opportunities as well as losses. Use the same rule across the sample and evaluate realised costs, ambiguous sequences and exceptional sessions separately from ordinary days.

sections.title: Express slippage in the same unit as the plan
sections.content:
For the invented 100 entry and 98 stop, planned risk is two points. If a fast-market stop-market exit is 97.5, the realised loss is 2.5 points before fees: 1.25 times the planned risk. Do not report it as exactly −1R simply because the original stop was two points away. A limit entry has different fill uncertainty from a market entry, and transaction costs may change during an event. A realistic replay records these assumptions rather than using the visual neatness of the setup to excuse them.

The opening range lesson explains when a reference becomes complete; the journaling lesson explains how to retain ambiguous results. Use Backtest Lab to inspect assumptions rather than awarding an automatic target-first outcome.

keyTerms.definition: Execution and direction can change again when the next information event occurs.
A candle reaches both levels without revealing their intrabar order.
The difference between the planned execution price and actual fill, which can enlarge a loss.
A predeclared reason to exclude an execution attempt while retaining the case for review.

summary: Check official release dates before the session.
Separate statement and press-conference stages.
Keep ambiguous and excluded cases in the journal.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Weekly Profiles: Context Without Prediction
quote: Use the developing week to organise scenarios, not to label Monday with knowledge of Friday.

sections.title: What does a weekly profile describe?
sections.content: A weekly profile is a framework for comparing the location and sequence of a week’s extremes, expansions and retracements. It is not twelve guaranteed weekday scripts. Begin with completed higher-timeframe ranges, the current week opening gap and scheduled events. At Monday’s open, the final weekly high and low do not exist yet. Distinguish a provisional expectation from a completed descriptive label, and keep the alternative continuation or reversal scenario visible.

sections.title: Worked week: update the thesis as evidence arrives
sections.content: Suppose the prior week spans 100–120 and the new week opens at 116. Monday trades 114–119. Tuesday exceeds 120, but Wednesday accepts back below it. A bearish scenario toward a selected lower reference can now be evaluated; Monday alone did not establish that path. In the contrast, Wednesday holds above 120 and continues to 124. Calling Tuesday the inevitable weekly high in both cases confuses a possible profile with knowledge of the outcome. Record the time when each scenario becomes plausible and the evidence that cancels it.

sections.title: All-time highs and the limits of Friday retracements
sections.content: At an all-time high, there may be no previously traded high above price on that chart history. That absence does not create a ceiling or eliminate the possibility of continuation. A TGIF-style Friday retracement is conditional; do not force it because the calendar says Friday. Define the completed expansion you are measuring and the selected retracement reference. A strong directional week can extend into its close, while another can reverse before Friday. Neither outcome should be erased from the study.

sections.title: Connect weekly context to a daily plan
sections.content: Use the weekly map to choose relevant objectives, then require a daily and intraday sequence for any separate setup. A weekly premium location does not authorise an immediate short. Journal the current quadrant, old extremes, NWOG, event calendar and the point that would invalidate the proposed path. Compare the same intraday model across different weekly conditions instead of mixing unrelated entries into one success rate. The historical URL retains its old name for continuity; this lesson replaces deterministic twelve-profile claims with evidence-based scenario work.

sections.title: Separate a daily draw from the weekly objective
sections.content:
A weekly objective can remain relevant while a particular day moves in the opposite direction. For example, a proposed move toward 100 does not prevent an intraday return from 114 to 118. A short entry aimed at the weekly level needs a timeframe, holding rule, protective reference and costs consistent with that horizon. Do not use a distant weekly objective to rescue an invalidated intraday idea. Review the weekly narrative and each daily setup independently, then ask whether their alignment improved the defined sample.

Use the PD array lesson to define the range and the opening range lesson for intraday timing. Backtest Lab can help keep an intraday entry test separate from a hindsight weekly narrative.

keyTerms.definition: A scenario based only on information currently available in the week.
A conditional end-of-week retracement study, not a Friday certainty.
A selected higher-timeframe destination that does not fix every daily path or validate an intraday entry.
The highest or lowest price observed so far, not necessarily the final high or low.

summary: Never use Friday’s completed extremes to justify Monday’s entry.
Keep continuation and reversal scenarios visible.
A weekly location still needs an intraday model.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Weekly Options: Payoffs and Risk Boundaries
quote: Understand the contract before interpreting the directional chart. This is a mechanics lesson, not an options recommendation.

sections.title: Why an options position is different from a futures position
sections.content: An option’s outcome depends on its underlying, strike, expiry, premium, multiplier and settlement terms. A correct directional idea can still lose if the move is too small or arrives too late. A short option collects a premium while taking an obligation; premium received is not the maximum possible loss. The 2025 options discussion introduces a bearish SPX call-writing idea. Studying that idea does not make uncovered selling suitable for a beginner or establish a reliable income method.

sections.title: SPX cash settlement is not share delivery
sections.content: SPX index options are cash-settled and European-style; product series can have different settlement timing. SPY ETF options have different exercise and delivery mechanics. Never transfer the rules from one to the other merely because both reference the S&P 500. Check the specific contract specifications, last trading time, expiry and settlement calculation. A hypothetical payoff chart at expiry says nothing about interim margin calls, changing option prices, liquidity or a broker’s risk controls.

sections.title: Worked payoff: an uncovered short call
sections.content: Use an invented index scale: strike 100, premium 2.5 and multiplier 100. At expiry, the short-call payoff before costs is [2.5 − max(settlement − 100, 0)] × 100. Settlement 99 gives 250; 102 gives 50; 110 gives −750. The break-even is 102.5 before costs. The maximum gain is the 250 premium, while losses have no fixed upper bound as the settlement rises. These are hypothetical arithmetic examples, not quoted SPX prices or a trade proposal.

sections.title: Contrast: a defined-width call credit spread
sections.content: For a hypothetical 100/105 call credit spread receiving 1.2 points, the maximum terminal gain is 120 and maximum terminal loss is 380 with a 100 multiplier, before costs. This assumes matched quantity, same expiry and the declared settlement mechanics. It is a different position from an uncovered call, not a way to describe that call as safe. Exercise, assignment, fees, liquidity and leg-management risks depend on the actual products. Keep the option contract study separate from the chart’s entry model and review the relevant risk disclosure first.

sections.title: Break-even and the cost of being only slightly right
sections.content:
For the invented short call, settlement at 102.5 exactly offsets the 2.5 premium before costs. A close just below that level can leave a small gross gain that fees erase. For the 100/105 spread receiving 1.2, terminal break-even is 101.2 before costs; above 105, the spread’s intrinsic width is five and its net loss is 3.8 points. The price of the options before expiry can behave differently from this terminal line. Read the payoff together with the contract terms, not as a live mark-to-market forecast.

Before comparing positions, review the market-mechanics chapter for underlying quotes, the event-risk chapter for execution uncertainty, and the journaling lesson for recording costs. None replaces an options contract specification or risk disclosure.

keyTerms.definition: A call-selling position whose rising-price loss is not capped by an offsetting hedge.
The contractual result at expiry under stated assumptions, before specified costs.
The contractual reference used to calculate an option’s exercise value.
The option price paid or received, distinct from the seller’s potential loss.
The factor converting quoted option points into contractual monetary amounts.

summary: Identify the actual option product and settlement terms.
Premium collected is not the loss limit.
A terminal payoff does not model the whole holding period.

part: Part IX - ICT 2025 Official Mentorship Curriculum
title: ICT Replay and Journaling: Study One Model Honestly
quote: A useful journal preserves decisions made before the outcome, including the days when the best decision was no trade.

sections.title: Turn the framework into a falsifiable study
sections.content: Choose one instrument, session, timeframe and model variant. Declare the context filter, recognition event, entry, failure condition, objective and expiry before replay. A first-presented FVG study is not interchangeable with a Venom or lunch-retracement study. The same 2025 lecture collection includes different approaches on different days; forcing every example into one rigid checklist distorts it. Start with a small coherent question, such as whether a candidate leaves a premarked balanced range, rather than collecting every named PD array at once.

sections.title: Pause, predict privately, then reveal
sections.content: Hide later candles and save the chart at the moment the reference becomes available. Write what you expect, why, what would contradict it and whether an order could already exist. Reveal the next interval and preserve the original note rather than editing it to match the outcome. Use a second image for the later result. Automatic captions help locate a source explanation but can mishear prices and terms; inspect the chart where a spoken detail matters and record unresolved ambiguity instead of guessing.

sections.title: Classify fills before calculating performance
sections.content: Separate no qualifying setup, qualifying but unfilled, completed win, completed loss and unresolved sequence. Suppose ten directional ideas include four that never return to entry, three completed +2R outcomes, two −1R outcomes and one ambiguous candle. The resolved filled subset has five trades and net +4R before costs; the four unfilled ideas are not four extra wins. The ambiguous case stays unresolved or follows a conservative predeclared assumption. This tiny invented sample demonstrates accounting, not evidence of a profitable method.

sections.title: Review costs, variations and source confidence
sections.content: Deduct the chosen commission and execution-cost model consistently, then inspect how the result changes across sessions, volatility and unseen examples. Record rejected candidates as well as selected ones. A source’s demonstration, an invented teaching sequence and an independently verified execution are different evidence types. The supplied library contains 83 recordings; selected caption passages were available for 75, while eight required visual-only review. That is a documented reading basis, not a claim that every spoken minute or model variation has been independently verified.

sections.title: A minimum journal record another learner could audit
sections.content:
Store the instrument and contract, feed, date, timezone, model version, completed context, candidate boundaries, recognition time, intended order, expiry, failure level and objective. Add screenshots before and after, actual fill evidence or a clearly labelled simulation assumption, costs and the final classification. Keep a separate field for interpretation: for example, likely liquidity is an inference, while a trade above an old high is observed. Version the rule if you change it, then reserve later examples for review rather than repeatedly tuning the same small set.

Review the first presented FVG and Venom lessons as separate model variants. Use Backtest Lab to audit one fixed set of assumptions, keeping unresolved outcomes and rejected candidates visible.

keyTerms.definition: A qualifying plan whose declared entry was never reached after recognition.
Whether a claim comes from a source example, a teaching invention or verified execution data.
The declared initial planned risk used to express outcomes; realised losses can exceed one R.
A saved specification of the study conditions, changed explicitly rather than rewritten after outcomes.

summary: Save the expectation before revealing later candles.
Separate unfilled and ambiguous cases from resolved trades.
Use one declared cost model and preserve rejected candidates.
